data.narrative:
Zanskar is a Series C climate and energy company founded by Carl Hoiland and Joel Edwards that has raised $180M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 3 same-stage, same-sector private peers (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy) plus 1 public comparable (LNZA), embedded within a broader frontier-tech climate set of 9 private and public companies.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The stage-progression method uses the $180M total raised as a base proxy and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage step-ups, implying a $306M valuation. The peer-median method anchors to the median valuation of the 3 same-sector, same-stage peers: $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals).

These methods triangulate to a valuation range of $260M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $653M. The wide dispersion reflects meaningful uncertainty around whether Zanskar's technology maturity, capital intensity, and path to revenue align more closely with the lower (Electric Hydrogen, Amogy) or upper (KoBold Metals) end of peer valuations. Stage progression and peer comparables diverge by approximately $700M, suggesting that capital raised alone is insufficient to narrow the range without clearer visibility into unit economics and technology risk.
